items.title: Building the next generation of Postgres contributors: what’s working & what’s getting in the way | Claire Giordano | Postgres Summit US 2026
items.summary: Slides from a conference talk at Postgres Summit US 2026 in New York City. Abstract: How do we build the next generation of Postgres contributors, and what’s getting in the way?The Postgres open source project celebrates 30 years in 2026. That’s a huge milestone, and also a good moment to think about the future. Because unlike commercial companies, open source projects don’t have legions of recruiters—and yet they still depend on a steady stream of new contributors.This talk is an update to one I gave earlier this year on the Main Track at FOSDEM, about building the next generation of open source contributors. In that talk, we looked at the Postgres project through three lenses: the soul, the machine, and the fuel. The Soul is the human ecosystem, the community, the culture of Postgres. The Machine is the workflows, tooling, decision-making, & governance. The Fuel is the economics & funding that underpin the open source project.If you depend on Postgres—and want it to be thriving a decade from now—this talk will give you a clearer picture of what’s working, where we have more work to do, and how you can have real impact on the future of the project.

items.title: A Secret Decoder Ring for Postgres Replication: A Beginner’s Guide | Claire Giordano | Postgres Summit US 2026
items.summary: Slides from a conference talk at Postgres Summit US 2026 in New York City. Abstract: If you’re new to Postgres, replication can feel like alphabet soup: logical, physical, streaming, synchronous, asynchronous—and that’s just the core features.This is the replication primer I wish I’d had when I first started working with Postgres. In this talk, we’ll break down the main types of replication—what’s actually different about them, how they work, and when you’d choose one over another. Expect diagrams, analogies, and zero sub-bullets as we map replication concepts to mental models you already know.We’ll connect each approach to real-world use cases: high availability (HA), disaster recovery (DR), scaling reads, and migrations. Along the way, we’ll demystify WAL (the write-ahead log) and touch on how HA setups like Patroni fit into the picture.If you’ve ever nodded along in a replication conversation while quietly looking up terms under the table, this talk is for you.
